availability_states.meaning: The package is supplied with its required fields present, and at least one of its fields is populated. A field is populated when its value is anything other than null, an empty string, an empty list, or an empty object. The same rule applies to every package, whether or not it has required fields.
The tool has no source for this package at all.
The tool has a source for this package and this case has nothing in it, so none of its fields is populated. That is a fact about the case, for example a claim with no children.
The data exists and was deliberately not shared with the review, for example by a consent or confidentiality decision.

data_packages.description: Information used to judge whether evidence is sufficient for the claim, rather than merely relevant to it.

field_meanings.acceptance_criteria: The criteria the evidence has to meet for the claim, such as pass conditions or required results.
field_meanings.configuration: The system, software, and sensor configuration the evidence applies to.
field_meanings.coverage: What the evidence covers and what it does not, such as conditions, functions, or hazards.
field_meanings.limitations: Known limitations, exclusions, and unfavourable results recorded for the evidence.
field_meanings.scenario_set: The scenarios, test cases, or data set the evidence was produced from, and where they came from.
field_meanings.thresholds: The numeric limits the results are judged against.

field_meanings.terms: Each project term used in the reviewed elements, with its definition.

data_packages.description: Linked external standard requirements or guidance references.

field_meanings.linked_requirements: Each external standard requirement or guidance clause linked to the reviewed elements, with its identifier and, where available, its text.

data_packages.description: Relevant review comments, prior findings, proposal history, and baseline or version state.

field_meanings.baseline: The baseline, version, or snapshot of the case the elements are reviewed in, and whether they changed since the last reviewed baseline.
field_meanings.prior_findings: Findings an earlier review, by a person or a tool, raised against the reviewed elements, each with its guideline id and status.
field_meanings.proposal_history: Changes proposed to the reviewed elements, and whether each was accepted, rejected, or is still pending.
field_meanings.review_comments: Remarks a person recorded against the reviewed elements, with author and date where known.

data_packages.description: A review concern or focus supplied by the user requesting the review.

field_meanings.review_intent: The concern or question the user asked the review to focus on, in the user's words.

document.purpose:
This document consolidates review guidance for safety cases into one
guideline-based review framework that can be cited during reviews.
document.title: Safety Case Core Guidelines

when_unavailable: Assess every guideline of the profile against the data that was supplied, and state in the result which packages were not available and in which state. A package that is empty tells the review that the case has nothing there, and the review may rely on that, for example to report that a claim has no path to evidence. A package that is not implemented or withheld tells the review nothing about the case. It never silences a guideline and is never by itself a finding against the argument, and the review does not infer what it would have contained. A profile's when_absent entry, where one is published, is the only exception. The rule is for the packages around the reviewed element; if the profile's selected-element package itself is not available, there is nothing to review, and the tool reports that no review was performed rather than an empty result.
